# Delta: cursor/fix-7161-agent-path (PR #7198) — merge-queue kick: 11 tests fail under the new resolver

PR #7198 was kicked from the merge queue (run 32669662236): shard 3/4 failed. Reproduced locally in your
worktree: `pytest -q tests/agent_runtime/test_acpx_adapter.py tests/ai_agent_bridge/test_ask_contract.py`
→ **11 failed, 206 passed**. Root cause: those tests monkeypatch `acpx_module.shutil.which` with one-arg
fakes (`lambda name: …`, `lambda _name: None` at test_acpx_adapter.py:2387/2467/2595/2633 and
test_ask_contract.py:574/599), and `binary_resolve.resolve_agent_binary` now calls
`shutil.which(binary, path=search_path)` → `TypeError: … unexpected keyword argument 'path'` → wrong
failure mode (missing-binary remediation never raised; confined-argv assertions fail).

## Outcome
The full runtime + bridge suites pass with the resolver in place, and the seam the tests rely on is a
deliberate, documented one — not an accident of `shutil.which`'s signature.

## Do (authoring lane's call on shape; state it in the commit body)
Either make the fakes conform to `shutil.which`'s real signature (`lambda name, *a, **k:`), or give
`binary_resolve` an explicit patchable seam (e.g. a module-level `_which = shutil.which` that tests
patch) and route the acpx call sites through it. Prefer the option that leaves future tests unable to
break the same way. No behaviour change to the resolver itself.

Fixed the 11 merge-queue failures by adding a patchable `_which` seam in `binary_resolve` and updating tests to target it instead of one-arg `shutil.which` fakes.

## Approach

`resolve_agent_binary` calls `shutil.which(binary, path=search_path)`. Tests that patched `acpx_module.shutil.which` with one-arg lambdas (`lambda name: …`) hit `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'path'` instead of the intended missing-binary refusal.

**Fix:** Added `binary_resolve._which = shutil.which` as a documented patch seam; `resolve_agent_binary` routes through it. Tests now patch `binary_resolve._which` (or both seams via `_patch_path_binary_lookup` when node PATH lookup is also faked). Resolver behavior is unchanged.
